title: Unified timeout, keep‑alive and connection pooling patterns for Python / TS / Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Define and ship cross-language, ergonomically sane transport presets and examples for connection pooling, TCP/HTTP keep‑alive, and request/stream timeout semantics in Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Goal: reduce customer confusion, lower operational connection churn, and improve streaming stability by 20% for long‑running chat sessions.
background: Multiple customers and internal integrations have reported noisy connection churn and surprising stream aborts when using default SDK settings. We lack a single cross‑SDK recommendation set that balances latency-sensitive short calls and long‑lived streaming sessions. Current SDKs expose knobs but defaults and examples diverge, making platform troubleshooting expensive.
acceptance_criteria: Publish language-specific transport presets (low-latency, balanced, streaming-optimized) with clear defaults in SDK constructors
Add example snippets for Python, TypeScript, and Go for both short RPCs and streaming use cases
Emit three transport telemetry metrics from SDKs: socket_reuse_rate, avg_idle_connection_seconds, and streaming_ping_missed_count
Document migration guidance and backward-compatibility notes; default changes must be behind opt-in config for one release
Benchmark: Reduce closed-by-server streaming aborts in our internal chat harness by >= 20% using streaming-optimized presets
proposal_summary: Introduce three named presets (latency, balanced, streaming). Each preset sets: connection_pool_max, connection_pool_min, idle_reap_seconds, tcp_keepalive_interval, http2_ping_interval, per_request_deadline, streaming_read_deadline, and backoff windows. Expose via SDK constructor arg and environment variable like REDWOOD_SDK_TRANSPORT_PRESET. Provide language-specific example config and rationale.
recommendations: Latency preset: small pool (2-4), aggressive idle reap (30s), short request deadline (10s), keepalive disabled to avoid extra pings on short calls
Balanced preset: medium pool (8), idle reap 120s, request deadline 30s, tcp keepalive 60s, http2 ping 120s

Streaming preset: pool size 16, min idle 4, idle reap 600s, tcp keepalive 30s, http2 ping 15s, streaming_read_deadline disabled at network layer but SDK-level soft heartbeat (application-level ping) every 25s
python_examples:
# constructor example
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(transport_preset="streaming", connection_pool_max=16, http2_ping_interval=15)
typescript_examples:
// fetch-style short call with deadline
await client.generate({ prompt, deadlineMs: 30000 })
// streaming via EventSource / fetch: use streaming preset, and attach reconnect/backoff handler that respects Retry-After from server
go_examples: // long streaming conn: set KeepAlive and MinIdleConns on http2.Transport and use context.WithTimeout for non-stream requests
// example backoff policy: use exponential jitter with base=150ms, max=5s, attempts=5
telemetry_and_dashboards: SDK emits metrics: sdk.socket_reuse_rate (percent), sdk.avg_idle_connection_seconds, sdk.streaming_ping_missed_count
Add dashboard panels: per-region socket_reuse_rate, streaming_abort_rate_by_preset, avg_request_latency_by_preset
Alert: streaming_ping_missed_count > 5 over 5m for a customer => investigate network middlebox interference
migration_notes: Do not change defaults immediately. Ship presets behind REDWOOD_SDK_TRANSPORT_PRESET and document next-release default switch plan
Provide a migration guide: how to toggle preset, how to detect if a workload should switch (high aborted streams, high connection churn), and rollback steps
Add e2e tests that run our internal chat harness against each preset to prevent regressions
tradeoffs_and_risks: Lower idle reaping reduces connection churn but increases per-customer socket usage and memory; Dedicated customers may need quota adjustments
Aggressive TCP keepalive/pings improve middlebox traversal but may increase network egress and tenant costs
Streaming preset keeps connections open longer which may worsen head-of-line blocking on constrained hosts; mitigate with higher pool sizes and multiplex-aware runtimes
implementation_plan: Week 1: finalize presets and update SDK option schemas; write examples for each language
Week 2: instrument telemetry in SDKs and add dashboard templates; land example docs and migration guide
Week 3: ship beta behind environment flag to canary orgs and run chat harness; collect metrics
Week 4: iterate on defaults and prepare release notes; roll out opt-in to wider users
open_questions: Should streaming preset enable HTTP/2 PING at transport layer or rely exclusively on app-level heartbeats?
What default connection_pool_max is appropriate for serverless Node.js users with ephemeral processes?
Do we want a per-route override API for SDKs (e.g., short calls use latency preset, chat route uses streaming preset) or keep it only client-level?
